messages:
maya: Heads up — got a reproducible failure in the onboarding sample-app when access tokens expire under load. Combination of token refresh races + 429s. Repro + logs below.

leo: Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro (curl or small snippet) and any 429 headers you observed?

maya: Repro steps I used:
1) Start sample-app with `--token-ttl=3s` to force frequent refreshes
2) Run `./repro.sh --clients=20 --duration=30s` which fires concurrent requests at /v1/chat
3) Watch the logs — many requests see 401, then subsequent inflight requests get 429s.

Logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-14T09:12:01Z] user=u99 request=aa1 status=401 msg="token expired"
[2026-02-14T09:12:01Z] user=u99 refresh.start
[2026-02-14T09:12:01Z] user=u99 request=bb2 status=429 Retry-After: 1
[2026-02-14T09:12:02Z] user=u99 request=cc3 status=429
[2026-02-14T09:12:03Z] user=u99 refresh.done token=tok_abc
[2026-02-14T09:12:04Z] user=u99 request=dd4 status=200 latency=38ms
```

maya: Notes: sometimes backend returns `Retry-After`; other times not. JS SDK silently retried the 429s and the app kept going, but Python SDK surfaced an error immediately in my smoke test so the onboarding sample failed. Also our runtime has a single-flight refresh, but the SDKs don't share that pattern, so multiple SDK clients tried to refresh at once.

sophie: Sounds like three items to address: (1) export/standardize a single-flight token refresh helper in all SDKs, (2) idempotency safe-replay defaults, and (3) consistent 429/backoff semantics across languages.

sam: For 429/backoff we should: if `Retry-After` header present, sleep exactly that many seconds; otherwise use exponential backoff with full jitter. Suggested algorithm:
```
base = 100ms
sleep = random(0, base * 2 ** attempt)
max_attempts = 5
```
This reduces thundering herd without blocking too long.

sophie: Parity detail: JS currently treats 429 as retryable by default; Python and Rust do not. New default should be: retry 429 only when the request is idempotent or an Idempotency-Key header is present. Provide opt-in `retryOn429` config for non-idempotent routes.

leo: On token refresh: we already have single-flight in the runtime. SDKs should implement the same pattern to avoid multiple concurrent refreshes. Example pseudocode to export from SDK auth helper:
```
let refreshInFlight = null
async function getToken() {
  if (token.ok) return token
  if (!refreshInFlight) refreshInFlight = doRefresh()
  await refreshInFlight
  refreshInFlight = null
  return token
}
```

maya: Adding `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` on client-side POSTs for user actions fixed the duplication in my run because the backend deduped repeated requests. But two operational notes: (a) backend TTL for idempotency records must be >= retry window (recommend 5m), (b) clients should be able to opt-out of auto-idempotency for certain developer flows.

sam: Also capture metrics so we can measure scope: `sdk.retries_total`, `sdk.retry_after_honored`, `sdk.duplicate_responses` and expose them in the Console. That will help quantify the impact.

maya: I pushed a tiny change in the onboarding repo that wraps the SDK with a single-flight token helper + auto idempotency for known endpoints. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/99 — includes `repro.sh` and README explaining how to run.

ci-bot: CI scheduled for PR #99 1 — running repro job on linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64. Will post pass/fail and flaky counts.

sophie: Action items: 1) Create SDK parity ticket (JS/Python/Rust) to standardize 429 semantics and add `retryOn429` flag; 2) Add `auth.singleFlight()` helper to all SDKs and document; 3) Docs page: "Retries, idempotency, and token refresh best practices" in devex docs; 4) Backend: increase idempotency key TTL to 5m default.

sam: I'll own metrics dashboard PR for retries and duplicate counts.

maya: I'll open the SDK parity tickets and link them to PR #99. Thanks for the quick triage and suggestions everyone. :thumbsup:
